dataflow.outcome: recoverable local denial of indexing and host resource pressure
dataflow.sink: KCS process heap, filesystem I/O, hash CPU, and scope store-lock availability
dataflow.source: attacker-controlled file size and contents in an operator-selected local scope
dataflow.summary: direct-child file length -> `entry.metadata().len()` -> unchecked `std::fs::read()` for raw hash -> preview candidate -> late `max_input_bytes` adapter skip

impact.why: The issue can deny indexing for the selected scope and stress host resources, but it is local, recoverable by removing the file, and does not cross a confidentiality or authorization boundary by itself.

likelihood.why: Once the operator indexes the supplied scope, the allocation path is deterministic and requires no timing race or unusual command.

limitations: Ignored files, non-regular entries, `.kcs`, `.kcsignore`, XDG state, and default-excluded Tier-A secrets do not enter this read.
The later cap still prevents oversized adapter normalization and network submission.

reachability.attacker: lower-trust content contributor to a selected local/shared scope
reachability.outcome: one indexing invocation can be delayed, aborted, or killed before useful adapter work begins
preconditions: The file is readable, regular, direct-child, and not ignored or secret-excluded.
The filesystem can present the chosen logical size; sparse-file support increases attacker efficiency.
reachability.summary: The attacker needs the ability to supply a readable, included regular direct-child file and the operator must run normal indexing rather than preview. No race, credential, network service, or elevated privilege is required.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust content contributor places an included oversized or sparse regular file as a direct child of a selected scope. When the operator runs ordinary non-preview indexing, KCS computes a raw hash by reading the whole file before the configured cap is checked, consuming memory, I/O, and hash CPU while the store lock is held.

codeEvidence.explanation: A normal `kcs index` call sets `include_raw_hashes` to true before the preview-mode early return. This makes scan-time hashing part of the ordinary non-preview path.
codeEvidence.label: Non-preview index requests scan raw hashes

codeEvidence.explanation: The contributor-controlled direct child must be a regular file, and KCS already has its logical `size_bytes` before any raw hash is computed. That value is the available pre-allocation decision point.
codeEvidence.label: Scanner records candidate length before hashing

codeEvidence.explanation: If the file is included, the raw-hash branch calls `std::fs::read(&path)` without checking `size_bytes` or streaming. The resulting owned byte vector creates `O(n)` heap growth before the configured cap can act.
codeEvidence.label: Raw hashing reads the complete file into memory

codeEvidence.explanation: KCS has a documented default size policy. The missing control is not the absence of a cap, but that the cap is not consulted before scan-time allocation.
codeEvidence.label: The input cap exists but is defined for the adapter policy

codeEvidence.explanation: This branch correctly prevents downstream adapter work for oversized files, but it iterates over an already-built preview. The raw-hash read has already happened.
codeEvidence.label: The cap is checked only after preview construction

codeEvidence.explanation: The existing regression proves the later adapter skip and uses a small file. It does not prove that scanning avoids a large or sparse pre-cap allocation.
codeEvidence.label: Existing test checks adapter skip, not scanner allocation

regressionTests: Create an included file larger than a tiny configured cap and assert the scanner does not allocate or hash the full file before deciding it is oversized.
Use a sparse file under a memory limit to prove logical file size is not materialized by scan hashing.
Keep preview, ignored-file, symlink, directory, `.kcs`, `.kcsignore`, XDG state, and Tier-A secret negative controls.
Verify streaming hash parity for ordinary small files.
remediation.summary: Enforce a scan-stage per-file or aggregate budget before any whole-file allocation, or replace raw hashing and CAS ingestion with bounded streaming. Keep the late adapter skip, but do not rely on it as the first resource-control point.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that KCS must enforce a per-file budget or stream hashing before allocating an included file's entire contents. `collect_direct_candidates()` already has `size_bytes`, but the raw-hash branch ignores it and calls `std::fs::read()`. `run_index_pipeline()` applies `max_input_bytes` only after `build_scan_preview()` returns, so the documented cap does not protect scan-time memory, I/O, or hash work.

summary: Normal non-preview `kcs index` asks the scanner to compute raw hashes. The scanner already records each included direct-child file's `metadata().len()`, but then calls `std::fs::read()` on the whole file before `adapter.policy.max_input_bytes` is consulted in the downstream indexing pipeline. An oversized or sparse regular file can therefore force proportional heap allocation, I/O, and hashing while the store lock is held.
title: Scan hashing allocates the full file before the input-size gate

assertions: An included direct-child regular file reaches raw-hash computation in normal non-preview indexing.
`metadata().len()` is available before the whole-file read, but no pre-read cap or streaming guard consumes it.
`adapter.policy.max_input_bytes` prevents adapter normalization and network submission only after scan preview construction.
The resource cost is proportional to the candidate's logical length for heap allocation, read I/O, and hashing work.
limitations: No high-memory or exhaustion experiment was performed.
Exact process termination thresholds depend on filesystem, allocator, OS policy, and available host memory.
Sparse-file behavior varies by filesystem, although the source-order allocation proof does not depend on sparseness.
validation.method: bounded existing cap test plus static source-order proof and safe local PoC
validation.summary: The saved validation traces normal `index` into `build_scan_preview()` with raw hashes enabled, then from `metadata().len()` to `std::fs::read()` with no intervening size decision, and finally to the downstream `max_input_bytes` skip. The included PoC verifies this ordering without running KCS or creating large inputs.
